consumer_reviews.affected_use: Facts L3 and Proof 2.1: composite map chi used to prove transitivity of pair identifications
consumer_reviews.exact_snippet: [L3] Transitivity of the pairwise identifications: for $\alpha,\beta,\gamma\in\mathcal X$ put $V:=\varphi_{\alpha\beta}^{-1}(U_{\beta\gamma})\subseteq U_{\alpha\beta}\subseteq U_\alpha$. Then $V$ is open and contains $j_0(\Sigma)$, and it carries a development structure of the same data: indeed $\varphi_{\alpha\beta}$ maps $V$ diffeomorphically onto $U_{\beta\gamma}\cap\varphi_{\alpha\beta}(U_{\alpha\beta})$, the intersection of two developments of the same data sharing the initial Cauchy surface, which is a development by [[lem-gr-intersection-of-developments]], and the development structure is transported by the data-fixing isometry $\varphi_{\alpha\beta}$ ([[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (a), [[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]]); consequently $\chi:=\varphi_{\beta\gamma}\circ\varphi_{\alpha\beta}|_V$ is a data-fixing isometric immersion of the development $V$ into $U_\gamma$, hence a data-fixing development embedding ([[lem-gr-data-fixing-immersion-is-embedding]] clauses (b)-(c)), so $(V,\chi)$ is a common subdevelopment of $\alpha,\gamma$ and therefore $V\subseteq U_{\alpha\gamma}$ and $\varphi_{\alpha\gamma}|_V=\chi$ ([[lem-gr-maximal-common-development]] clause (b)).
